MOLECULAR ONCOLOGY LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Cancer Center

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
MRN: [redacted ID]
DOB: [redacted date]
Specimen ID: [redacted ID]
Physician: Dr. [redacted name]

SPECIMEN INFORMATION
Specimen Type: Bone Marrow Aspirate
Collection Date: [redacted date]
Received Date: [redacted date]
Report Date: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INDICATION
Diagnostic sample assessment for suspected acute myeloid leukemia

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Real-Time PCR for CBFB::MYH11 Fusion Transcript

METHODOLOGY
RNA was extracted from bone marrow aspirate using standard protocols. cDNA synthesis was performed using random hexamer primers. Real-time quantitative PCR (qPCR) was performed using TaqMan technology on the Applied Biosystems 7500 Real-Time PCR System. The CBFB::MYH11 type A fusion transcript was amplified using specific primers and probe sets. Results are expressed as fusion transcript copy number per 100,000 copies of the ABL1 control gene. The analytical sensitivity of this assay is 1 fusion transcript per 100,000 ABL1 copies.

RESULTS

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Target                │ Copy Number        │ Normalized to ABL1     │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ CBFB::MYH11 Type A   │ 1.12 × 10^5       │ 55,755 / 100,000      │
│ ABL1 Control         │ 2.01 × 10^5       │ Reference Gene         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

INTERPRETATION
High levels of CBFB::MYH11 type A fusion transcript detected.

The presence of the CBFB::MYH11 fusion transcript is consistent with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with inv(16)(p13;q22) or t(16;16)(p13;q22). This genetic abnormality results from the inversion or translocation involving chromosome 16, leading to fusion of the core binding factor beta gene (CBFB) at 16q22 with the smooth muscle myosin heavy chain gene (MYH11) at 16p13.

The detected fusion transcript level of 55,755 copies per 100,000 ABL1 copies represents a high tumor burden at diagnosis. This baseline measurement will be important for monitoring minimal residual disease (MRD) during and after therapy.

CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE
AML with inv(16)/t(16;16); CBFB::MYH11 is classified as AML with recurrent genetic abnormalities according to WHO classification. This subtype generally has a favorable prognosis with appropriate therapy, particularly when combined with high-dose cytarabine-based regimens. The presence of this fusion transcript confirms the diagnosis and provides a molecular marker for MRD monitoring.

RECOMMENDATIONS
1. Results are consistent with AML with inv(16)/t(16;16); CBFB::MYH11 diagnosis
2. Next paired bone marrow (5ml first pull in EDTA) and peripheral blood (20ml in EDTA) samples for MRD assessment post-therapy
3. Serial monitoring of CBFB::MYH11 transcript levels is recommended to assess treatment response
4. A 3-log reduction from baseline is considered a good molecular response

REPORTED BY
[redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Director, Molecular Oncology Laboratory

Electronically signed on [redacted date]
